title: Embedded SDK platform contracts & bootflow sketch
content:
Context:
This is a working sketch for a compact developer-facing "platform contract" that defines expectations between the Redwood serving/runtime surface and embedded SDKs (mobile/edge/sidecar). The goal is to produce a one-page checklist + bootflow that integrators can follow for 0->demo in ~30 minutes and engineers can use to gate merges and QA.

Audience:
- SDK engineers (mobile/edge/sdk team)
- Integrators / solutions engineers building sampleapps
- Field/support first responders

Primary constraints we care about:
- Latency and token-cost friendly defaults (batching + short timeouts)
- Deterministic failure surface (clear error codes, stable retry semantics)
- Minimal auth/credential surface for quickstarts (dev mode) + clear migration path to production (KMS/HSM, per-route keys)
- Observable by default: traces, token counts, cold-start markers

One-page platform contract (developer obligations + runtime guarantees):
- SDK exposes a single init(apiKey, options) that returns a singleton client. Init is idempotent and cheap.
- Platform guarantees: hosted/dev endpoints return stable error codes: 4xx (client), 429 (rate), 5xx (platform), 524 (gateway-timeout). Documented mapping in README.
- Default timeouts: request-level = 12s, stream handshake = 8s. Configurable per-client.
- Offline/sim mode: all SDKs ship a hermetic simulator (local stub) that returns recorded golden responses for the quickstart flows.
- Telemetry: SDK must emit 3 events per request: request.start, request.end (with token_count), request.fallback (if triggered). Events must include route/model_id and latency_ms.
- Fallback policy: client may attempt up to 1 automatic fallback to a compatible model variant when receiving 5xx within 250ms of response; otherwise surface to app.

Bootflow (0->30m demo path):
1) Dev account prep (1-3m)
   - Sign up, generate API key (dev tier), copy to clipboard.
2) Local project init (5m)
   - git clone sampleapp-embedded (link in linked_artifacts), run `yarn install`/`pip install -r requirements.txt`.
   - Place API key into `.env.dev` (example provided).
3) Hermetic smoke run (3m)
   - run `./devstub start` (bundled with SDK) -> returns pre-recorded prompts/responses.
   - Confirm sample UI shows expected output.
4) Switch to hosted endpoint (5m)
   - flip `ENV=hosted` in `.env.dev`, run sample. Validate telemetry shows request.start/end in console or dev dashboard.
5) Observe failure & fallback (4m)
   - Use `DEV_FAULT=short-5xx` to simulate a platform error and validate fallback behavior and error propagation in sample UI.
6) Quick instrumentation check (5m)
   - Open dev console, confirm token_count logged, latency_ms plausible, and no PII in telemetry payload.

Acceptance checklist for an SDK build / PR gate:
- [ ] init() documented and idempotent (unit tests exist)
- [ ] default timeouts applied and configurable via options object
- [ ] hermetic stub present and runnable via a single command
- [ ] telemetry events emitted for each request with model_id and token_count
- [ ] documented error mapping table in README (examples for each code)
- [ ] CI smoke test that runs hermetic stub and asserts quickstart success within 30s
- [ ] sampleapp has a minimal e2e that toggles between stub and hosted and asserts telemetry/events

Developer notes / anti-patterns to avoid:
- Do not lazily create the client on first request in long-lived environments; prefer explicit init to control keys/telemetry.
- Avoid exponential backoff with large multipliers for UI flows—use a capped linear backoff for short quickstart UX.
- Don’t log full prompt contents to telemetry in dev builds (masking rule default).

Edge cases and unresolved questions (open issues):
- How to represent token_count consistently across models with different tokenizers? (Proposal: standardize on UTF-8 byte approximation in telemetry and flag model-specific token estimates in model metadata.)
- Should the hermetic stub include fuzzed latency profiles to better simulate cold starts? PRO: realistic testing. CON: flaky quickstart demos.
- SDK binary size targets for mobile: target < 2MB additional compressed for core runtime shim — needs SRE/infra input.

Short sample snippets (pseudo):
- JS init example:
  const client = RedwoodSDK.init(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, { timeoutMs: 12000, telemetry: true });
  const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rwd-compact-1', prompt: 'Summarize this...' });

- Telemetry sample event (logged):
  request.start { request_id: "abc123", model_id: "rwd-compact-1", ts: 1691234567 }
  request.end   { request_id: "abc123", tokens: 21, latency_ms: 213 }

Implementation plan (next steps):
- Prototype hermetic stub packaging (owner: Liam) — sprint 1
- Draft README contract and error table (owner: Samira) — sprint 1
- Add CI smoke runner that hits stub and validates sampleapp output (owner: Priya) — sprint 2
- Cross-team review with infra/serving runtime to lock defaults (meeting invite: TBC)

Short TODO (this doc):
- [ ] Finalize token_count format and update linked artifacts
- [ ] Add mobile binary-size target & signoff owner
- [ ] Add sampleapp repo link to linked_artifacts once created

Slack threads / references:
- Slack: #devexp (thread: "embedded-quickstart-contracts")
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/412 (telemetry hooks)
- Jira: JIRA-DEVEXP-1283 (stub packaging)

Notes to reviewer:
This is intentionally compact — the product/infra teams want a minimal readable contract that SDK engineers can follow without sifting through design docs. Happy to expand any section if reviewers prefer more examples or stricter gating criteria.
